Nahoon Estuary

By: Tarryn Crossman | Paid

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
The Nahoon Esturay nature reserve, the heart and soul of east-london in the eastern cape, is being slowly being destroyed by sewerage that is leaking in to the Estuary from old over used pipes and broken pump stations. We meet the people who are taking the buffalo city municipality to court to fight for the survival of the local tourist treasure

Further information:
The Nahoon Estuary Nature reserve in east-london is 25 hectares of forest, beach, natural ponds, and mangroves that are being destroyed by sewerage. In December 2021 the e-Coli levels in the estuary were sitting at 28 0000/100ml they are supposed to be around 500/100ml



In 2019 the Buffalo city municipality together with Christo Theart, from NPO Nahoon Estuary Management Forum, adopted a management plan for the estuary. But over the past 3-years, the plan has not been allocated a budget and the municipality has not implemented any part of the extensive plan leaving the estuary in a desperate state



Christo, and his volunteer team, eventually stopped trying to work with the municipality and started taking them to court.

The first court order that they won was for the municipality to fix a broken pump station that had been broken for over 3 years, overflowing sewerage straight into the estuary. As a result, there is a water hyacinth overload in that area

2 years ago, someone was contracted to clear the hyacinths, they were never paid so they left. Residents are now clearing it.

Legally, hyacinth is a category 1d, which means by law it must be removed



2nd action - pump station at a group housing development - Maldives

Sewage moving into a stream under the N2 and into the estuary

Order was just given for the municipality to fix it – they still have 120 days left to complete the court order



3rd action - to get the municipality to stop using streams along the housing side of the estuary to dump sewerage overflow directly into the estuary.

the municipality claim that the pump here is blocked with silt as the silt filter is not effective enough for the increased amount of sewerage, so it overflows. they know the problem, they just haven't gotten around to fixing it in over 5 years.

a court order has been granted order them to stop the overflow.



4th court action that is currently underway: two streams are constantly running sewerage from an informal settlement into the estuary

Christo has tested the streams and has the test results to prove it is pure sewerage, he also has the video of the streams running.

The municipality claim this can’t be solved as the informal settlement has been built over the existing sewerage pipes for that area.



the main sewerage pipes running right across the Estuary are copper pipes from the 1950s and are too small for east-Londons current population size, so the sewerage overflow is regularly released into the estuary. Christo has vn from people inside the municipality confirming this.



This nahoon estuary flows into the sea, where the beach is constantly been closed due to sewerage stills, as per the pics attached.



We have Affidavits of people that have gotten sick by using the nahoon river

No studies have been done with regards to the fish and birds



if we do it right this can be a great story about civilians taking on the government and winning. don't moan stand up and take action kinda thing.

Script:


Brendon Thomson brought his kids up on this river, his son Tyane started paddling when he was a toddler

He started paddling in nappies. Literally

After over ten years of water sports in the Nahoon Estuary, Tyane became seriously ill.

he got a bacterial infection from the E.coli in the water, which resulted in him having ended up in hospital.

But Tayne wasn’t the only paddle skier getting sick, South African champions
Tyde Malherbe and Daniel van-zyl smit have both gotten bacterial infections after training in the Nahoon Estuary

Daniel
and it’s not about being three days sick, it’s about being three days sick. And then maybe four days of being like, really tired So it’s a week of training
takes time out of our training and that’s like hinders our long term programs.
00:01:55:03 - 00:02:05:22
When I started, the water was always clear. I could see, like the water in the fish, filming was always beautiful, and it's like some mornings doing a paddle. I can just smell sewage

For years the Nahoon estuary in the East-Cape has been a haven for water sport enthusiast, and Elite athletes from around the world, but when sewage started flowing into the river, the water quality began to deteriorate

15 years ago, Merrifield School, had a midfield mile they stopped it because it was just too polluted for people to use it.

Retired town planner, Christo Theart volunteered to help the municipality work on a solution to ensure this Estuaries future, but unfortunately after two years of all talk and no action Christo, together with other steak holders, are now taking the municipality to THE high court . over the past year they have won 3 high court orders against BUFFALO city municipality to stop the illegal spillage of sewerage into the Nahoon estuary


CHRISTO:
we decided that It is time for something different And we started our first court case against the municipality, which was successful.

Christo and is colleagues have a filed a 4th high court application against the buffalo city municipality, demanding that they stop the sewage spills from Nompomelelo in this area of the Estuary. It is due to be heard on March the 22nd.
Sam Ngwenya is the spokesperson for the buffalo city municipality

00:25:50:12 - 00:26:14:16
the estuary itself, it's such a magical place. It's so beautiful here.
00:26:17:08 - 00:26:25:11
That it's something worth fighting for, I think,

Torquey road is one of the most affluent areas in East-London, these are the cities top rate payers, it is also one of the hotspots where sewerage is overflowing into the Estuary

MAC AND CHRISTO
You can smell it. Oh my god, here it is. Oh goodness. Oh, it’s madness.
It’s bad. It’s bad. It’s bad.
I mean, I didn't I didn't think it was this bad
It’s actually unbelievable to imagine that you've paid millions of rands to live in a place like this and every day, this is the smell that you greeted with. I don't even want to breathe.

According to Christo these pipes are carrying sewage to the nearby Nahoon pump station, but because THE BUFFALO CITY POPULATION HAS DOUBLED IN THE PAST TWENTY YEARS these sewage pipes can no longer handle all the residents waste. So instead of building an overflow dam to contain the sewage until it can be disposed of, the municipality simply build a purpose-made overflow directly into this stream which illegally flows directly into the nahoon estuary.
This stream of sewage also flow through Resident Pumilelele BALFOURS MULTI-MILLION RAND HOME

PUMI INTERVIEW: See more Pumi in this interview
when did you start living here
This is the way back in 2012. We could see a nice stream running through the property and there’d be FISH... A stingray was here one time. But now with all this grey water not a chance, not a chance.

MAC and Pumi – name check
So you wouldn’t jump off here, like in the movies
Definitely not
I mean, if you fall into the water in deep trouble.

TO COMPLY WITH THE LAW, e-coli LEVELS for recreational waters MUST BE less that 500 counts per 100milliletres , last year on average the readings in the Nahoon estuary were 6 x that amount and at some point the reading were 28 000/100ml that is 56x over, SO ANY HUMANS THAT COME INTO CONTACT WITH THE HIGHLY TOXIC WATER, COULD POTENTIALLY GET SICK

Although Brendons sons doctors couldn’t confirm it, Tayne had SPENT SO MUCH TIME IN THE RIVER, that they believed that his bacterial infection was from the extremely high e-coli levels in the Nahoon river which llanded Tayne in ICU. ”

It started attacking his organs. It actually got to the point where it attacked his pericardium, which is the lining around the heart.
And he ended up having a heart operation
He nearly died

Water Hyacinth is an invasive alien plant that thrives off PHOSPHATES – WHICH IN THIS CASE IS HUMAN FECAL MATTER, it is a tell tale sign that a river is IN distress. Until a few weeks back this whole area of the river was SMOTHERED wall to wall in Water Hyacinth WHICH GROW EXTERMELY RAPIDLY IN SEWAGE, SUFFOCATING PLANTS ANd ANIMALS, but they have since been washed out to sea

Julie: 00:03:10:17 - 00:03:36:00
the amount of sewage that is currently flowing into the system is fertilizing these plants and has allowed them to take over the system.
Without these sewage spills, we wouldn't have these invasive species.

Professor Julie Coetzee is the deputy director of the centre for biological control at Rhodes University, she has been studying the effect of these invasive plant species on this eco-system for years
How detrimental is that to the aquatic life here to the ecosystem of the estuary?
they're growing out and they covering the entire surface
What that does is it blocks light penetrating the water column, and light is essential for life in the water body.
No light penetrating, no oxygen is being produced and we say that the system is becoming completely. Anoxic. And so your indigenous fish are dying off, the plants are dying off
The river will die.

Besides Torque road the other big hotspot is here where sewerage is entering the Estuary from a nearby low income housing settlement, Nompumelelo

Christo and mac on the boat:
This is the culvert that brings the stormwater from Nompumelelo
that contains a lot of sewage. They take water tests regularly every week, and this area is the worst in the whole estuary.

Christo and is colleagues have a filed a 4th high court application against the buffalo city municipality, demanding that they stop the sewage spills from Nompomelelo in this area of the Estuary. It is due to be heard in March.
Sam Ngwenya is the spokesperson for the buffalo city municipality

SAM:
the people in Nompumelelo have built on top of that sewer line. But the plan for that before we even talk about the line is to actually find them housing and relocate them... We've found land where we can actually relocate those people so that we can resolve that problem.



Moving over 20 000 people is no easy task and although the buffalo city municipality has the land in place, they are still in the process of requesting funding from the national government, at the time of broadcast Ngwenya wasn’t sure what the actual budget is, but in the interim he says they are trying to improve the existing sewage infrastructure in Nompomelelo to prevent the spills into the Estuary

SAM: 1
00:11:12:07 - 00:11:29:16
Yes, at the moment, it's a big challenge for everyone concerned, but ultimately we have to find a long term solution for them
0:11:30:25 - 00:11:42:06
by allowing sewage to go straight in the river you are breaking the law. Yes, it is breaking the law. We agree on that. So I am continuing to do it.
00:11:42:26 - 00:12:13:22
I wouldn't say we're breaking the law. Remember you just said yes. No, no. I want to. I want to be specific on this. If people are vandalizing our pump station, if people are throwing foreign object on our pump station we fix it every day
00:12:13:25 - 00:12:17:01
But there are mitigating factors, and that's what I'm trying to show in this instance,

Regardless of the mitigating factors According to Law 26 of the municipalities by-laws, the discharge of sewage into any public space or storm drain is illegal.

The following day we returned to the area around Torquey road, as christo had received a tip off that there was an increased amount of sewage pouring into the estuary from the overflow system

So I don’t know whether we lucky or unlucky, because today we’ve come back and it’s flowing.
They've got six months to do something about this year 6 month
Because this can't go on like this, it has to stop, it has to stop.

On the 27th of January the high court ordered the municipality to provide an alternative to the Purpose-made overflow system on Torquay road, within 180 days. According to Ngwenya they have subsequently received a 1 million rand grant to upgrade this sewage infrastructure, which will solve the problem. He confirmed this will be completed within the deadline of their court order

MAC: does the city even know how much tourism it would bring?. it doesn't take a genius to figure out that if we can solve this problem, we can actually bring more money into the municipality. Is there no one in this entire municipality that sees that?
SAM: I agree with that, all of us want to see that place in a better place than it is right now.
I think the issue here is mainly speed.

Malherbe and Daniel van-zyl smit
Without this river I wouldn’t have found paddeling blab la
This river is amazing its sad

mac:
When will the Buffalo City Municipality say normal sewage into the known history? Is it even possible?
Sam: if we to just relocate the pipe system in there will need 200 million for that area only.
But we don't have to be a million sitting somewhere in the coffers of the municipality


Under-resourced and under pressure, can the municipality fix the ageing sewage infrastructure and prevent more illegal spills into the Nahoon estuary?

SAM It's a daunting task, but it's got to be sorted out in piecemeal
to do it all will take two years
Two years sam
Yes

MAC: how long will you fight this for
Christo: the water quality of the estuary is non-negotiable. It has to improve.
And we will not stop until that happens.

Julie:
Water is our most precious resource and is our most impacted resource
our water systems are hugely threatened.
we thrive when our rivers thrive? There's that whole saying water is life and without clean, healthy aquatic ecosystems. I think our connection with nature almost is lost

metadata.Summary: The Nahoon Esturay nature reserve, the heart and soul of east-london in the eastern cape, is being slowly being destroyed by sewerage that is leaking in to the Estuary from old over used pipes and broken pump stations. We meet the people who are taking the buffalo city municipality to court to fight for the survival of the local tourist treasure
metadata.Further information: The Nahoon Estuary Nature reserve in east-london is 25 hectares of forest, beach, natural ponds, and mangroves that are being destroyed by sewerage. In December 2021 the e-Coli levels in the estuary were sitting at 28 0000/100ml they are supposed to be around 500/100ml In 2019 the Buffalo city municipality together with Christo Theart, from NPO Nahoon Estuary Management Forum, adopted a management plan for the estuary. But over the past 3-years, the plan has not been allocated a budget and the municipality has not implemented any part of the extensive plan leaving the estuary in a desperate state Christo, and his volunteer team, eventually stopped trying to work with the municipality and started taking them to court. The first court order that they won was for the municipality to fix a broken pump station that had been broken for over 3 years, overflowing sewerage straight into the estuary. As a result, there is a water hyacinth overload in that area 2 years ago, someone was contracted to clear the hyacinths, they were never paid so they left. Residents are now clearing it. Legally, hyacinth is a category 1d, which means by law it must be removed 2nd action - pump station at a group housing development - Maldives Sewage moving into a stream under the N2 and into the estuary Order was just given for the municipality to fix it – they still have 120 days left to complete the court order 3rd action - to get the municipality to stop using streams along the housing side of the estuary to dump sewerage overflow directly into the estuary. the municipality claim that the pump here is blocked with silt as the silt filter is not effective enough for the increased amount of sewerage, so it overflows. they know the problem, they just haven't gotten around to fixing it in over 5 years. a court order has been granted order them to stop the overflow. 4th court action that is currently underway: two streams are constantly running sewerage from an informal settlement into the estuary Christo has tested the streams and has the test results to prove it is pure sewerage, he also has the video of the streams running. The municipality claim this can’t be solved as the informal settlement has been built over the existing sewerage pipes for that area. the main sewerage pipes running right across the Estuary are copper pipes from the 1950s and are too small for east-Londons current population size, so the sewerage overflow is regularly released into the estuary. Christo has vn from people inside the municipality confirming this. This nahoon estuary flows into the sea, where the beach is constantly been closed due to sewerage stills, as per the pics attached. We have Affidavits of people that have gotten sick by using the nahoon river No studies have been done with regards to the fish and birds if we do it right this can be a great story about civilians taking on the government and winning. don't moan stand up and take action kinda thing.
